classification.difficultyReason: Check non-negativity and calculate rectangular or triangular areas to test whether each total area is 1.

content.prompt: Which of the following graphs are probability density functions?

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular density outline with positive axis arrows, no grid and only the source numerical labels.
spec.mathematics: Constant height 1/6 between x=1 and x=7; vertical boundary segments meet the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is permanently visible; its area calculation and conclusion are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$f(x)\ge0$ throughout the displayed domain.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac16(7-1)\\&=\frac16\times6\\&=1\end{align*}$$
Therefore, it is a valid PDF.

spec.description: Horizontal density segment from the vertical axis to x=12, followed by a vertical boundary down to the horizontal axis; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Constant height 1/10 on the displayed interval from 0 to 12.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is permanently visible; its area calculation and conclusion are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac1{10}\times12\\&=\frac{12}{10}\\&\ne1\end{align*}$$
Therefore, it is not a PDF.

spec.description: Straight decreasing density segment from the labelled vertical intercept to the labelled horizontal intercept, without grid or extra ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is permanently visible; its area calculation and conclusion are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$f(x)\ge0$ throughout the displayed domain.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12\times20\times\frac1{10}\\&=1\end{align*}$$
Therefore, it is a valid PDF.

spec.description: Triangular density outline with an unlabelled interior apex toward the right. The apex horizontal placement is schematic and supplies no numerical given.
spec.mathematics: Triangle above the x-axis with base from 0 to 9 and maximum height 1/9; the apex x-coordinate is unspecified and unnecessary for its area.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is permanently visible; its area calculation and conclusion are answer-only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12\times9\times\frac19\\&=\frac12\\&\ne1\end{align*}$$
Therefore, it is not a PDF.
